title: Pre-Consumer Waste recycling
fullPassage: Pre-Consumer Waste is "waste" that is generated by the industrial processes used to make the products or packaging that we buy as consumers. This is manufacturing "waste" and is typically very clean, of consistent quality and comprises only a single material. Examples are: offcuts from aluminium cans; cardboard boxes or clothing; trimmings from prepreparing vegetables; or wood or textile offcuts from making furniture. Such "waste" was in the past often sent for disposal, but increasingly producers are recycling their internal "waste" to save money by turning unwanted trimmings or offcuts back into useable raw materials. As a result, the materials that end up in our finished products represent a surprisingly small amount of what we originally took from the earth. To send such materials for disposal is not only poor financial practice by the producer, from an environmental perspective it is criminal. These are good-quality, clean and easily collectable materials that just happen to be in the wrong form: so recycle or recover them!
